evidence.claim: 4 online authorizations under $10 within an hour, then a $236.28 purchase

Customer C09582 disputes transaction 3660350 ($236.28); a dispute is strong but not conclusive evidence (in the Round 1 review 7 of 8 customer reports were confirmed fraud, and one was cleared because the purchase fitted the cardholder)
Purchaser email domain gmail.com is this account's own: 4 earlier transactions on card C09582-K1 in its region 476 used it
$236.28 is 2.2 times the largest earlier purchase on card C09582-K1 in its region 476
Online purchase on a card whose history is 99% in person (708 earlier transactions)
Policy applied, Fraud Policy R2: Customer denies the transaction: Recommend BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE.
Pattern definition, Known fraud patterns: Card testing: A stolen card number is checked before use: three or more tiny online authorizations, often under $5, then a larger purchase.

case.summary: Alert HHF-007 was triggered when customer C09582 disputed online transaction 3660350 for $236.28 on card C09582-K1. The investigation revealed four online authorizations under $10 within an hour followed by the $236.28 purchase, which is 2.2 times the largest earlier purchase on card C09582-K1 in its region 476. In contrast, the purchaser email domain gmail.com matches the account's own domain, as seen in four earlier transactions on the card in region 476. The verdict is fraud with a fraud probability of 0.94. The final actions are to block the card and create a case.
